title: K-wise independence fools a monomial
statement: Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, and let $\mu$ be a probability distribution on $\{0,1\}^n$ such that every set of at most $k$ coordinates has a uniform joint distribution. For any set $S$ of at most $k$ coordinates, the expectation under $\mu$ of the monomial that is $1$ exactly when every coordinate in $S$ is $1$ equals its expectation under the uniform distribution on $\{0,1\}^n$.
hypotheses_covered: Probability distribution mu on the n-dimensional Boolean cube
Every coordinate set of size at most k has uniform joint distribution under mu
Coordinate set S has size at most k
